questions.q: What four stages does the lesson describe as the typical (though not universal) Administrator interview sequence?
options: Recruiter phone screen, hiring manager interview, technical round, and sometimes a panel
A written exam, a reference check, and nothing else
Only a single technical round, with no recruiter or manager involvement
A live coding test followed directly by an offer
questions.explain: The lesson lists a recruiter screen, a hiring manager interview, a technical round, and an occasional panel as the common stages, while noting not every company runs all four.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what are interviewers actually grading when they ask a record-visibility troubleshooting question?
options: Whether you can recite the exact governor limit numbers
How quickly you can say any plausible-sounding answer
The order you check things in -- object/field access, OWD, role hierarchy and sharing rules, then manual/Apex sharing
Whether you know the exact release notes for the current Salesforce version
questions.explain: The lesson emphasizes that the troubleshooting order, not a single guessed answer, is what's being evaluated.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say a validation rule versus Flow question matters in an interview?
options: Because Flow has been fully deprecated
Because validation rules can never run on a record
Because only developers are ever asked this question
Because it tests whether you know when a simple tool suffices versus when logic is complex enough to need Flow
questions.explain: The lesson frames this as a judgment question about choosing the right tool for the complexity of the logic, not a trick question with one tool always being correct.

questions.q: What does the lesson recommend doing with the LTV Customer Management System capstone when answering interview questions?
options: Use it as a source of specific, real examples -- a migration decision, a security choice, a growth story, a pushback story
Avoid mentioning it since it's just a class project
Memorize its code structure verbatim and recite it regardless of the question
Only mention it if directly asked about coursework
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly recommends pulling specific, real examples from the capstone rather than giving generic answers.

questions.q: The lesson describes one behavioral scenario involving an executive requesting access that violates policy. What is this question testing?
options: Whether you know Apex syntax
Whether you can tactfully push back while still upholding governance
Whether you're willing to grant any access an executive asks for
Whether you can configure a sandbox refresh
questions.explain: The lesson notes that this type of question evaluates your ability to push back tactfully and uphold governance, not simply comply.
